current: Delaney–Sun Valley and Redhawk were studied as two Transition clusters and merged from 2024 on. Almost all cost in this area is POI station work at Delaney, Sun Valley, Redhawk and the new TS30 500 kV switchyard. The only shared system upgrades are the Sun Valley–Hassayampa Tap 5-ohm reactor (Q467) and the 2025 Redhawk–Hassayampa 15-ohm reactors. Purple columns mark the APS planned transmission each cluster was studied against: the Outer Circle 230 kV build-out has been contingent since Transition Ph1, while the Rudd 500/230 kV bank and the Independence (TS21) package became contingent only from the 2024 cluster (Nov 2025). Transition reports modeled Jojoba–Rudd out.
2025-ph2a: With Q582 and Q605 out, the Redhawk–Hassayampa 15-ohm series reactors ($15M, short-circuit driven) are split among Q580, Q595 and Q617. Q617 (1,000 MW) carries $85M of station work for its own POI.
cluster-2026: 8 requests (5.2 GW, of which 2.2 GW NRIS), most at the proposed TS30 500 kV switchyard. Q652, Q653 and Q655 are 1,000 MW ERIS each. Q572 (1,300 MW), which was paying $31M to build TS30 in the 2024 cluster, has since withdrawn.
